purpose: Quantify the common cross-species A x H effect magnitude that the frozen Paper 2 design would detect with 80% and 90% probability under the actual temporal/observation layout and the realized preregistered permutation critical value.

inferential_anchor.rejection_rule: same one-sided alpha=0.05 paper-level rule as the frozen primary test
inferential_anchor.critical_value: derive exactly from the 9999 frozen paper-level permutation statistics; a synthetic statistic is detected when its frozen permutation p-value would be <=0.05

simulation.truth: same gamma_AH in all three species; gamma_A=0

summaries: raw detection fraction and Wilson 95% interval at each frozen effect-grid point
median fitted cross-species gamma_AH at each effect
for MDE interpolation only, fit a nondecreasing isotonic regression to detection fraction versus absolute gamma_AH magnitude using equal replicate weights
MDE80 and MDE90 by linear interpolation on that frozen isotonic curve between adjacent effect magnitudes
interpretation_boundary: This is a post-inference operating-characteristic analysis, not a new hypothesis test.
The realized permutation critical value is conditioned on the frozen observed design/outcomes; call the result a retrospective detectable-effect threshold, not prospective design power.
No effect grid point is chosen or removed based on the observed p=0.0947.
This analysis cannot turn a non-significant observed effect into evidence for absence; it only bounds which common-effect magnitudes the study was well positioned to detect.
Raw detection fractions are always shown; isotonic smoothing is used only to stabilize interpolation of the operating-characteristic threshold.
